passages.text: As a prisoner in the Lord, then, I urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling you have received: with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love, and with diligence to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.
passages.sermon:
I am a prisoner in the Lord.
I urge you to live in a way that is worthy of the calling you have received.
Live with all humility.
Live with gentleness.
Live with patience.
Bear with one another in love.
Work hard to keep the unity of the Spirit.
Keep this unity through the bond of peace.
passages.original: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς ἐγὼ ὁ δέσμιος ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀξίως περιπατῆσαι τῆς κλήσεως ἧς ἐκλήθητε μετὰ πάσης ταπεινοφροσύνης καὶ πραΰτητος μετὰ μακροθυμίας ἀνεχόμενοι ἀλλήλων ἐν ἀγάπῃ σπουδάζοντες τηρεῖν τὴν ἑνότητα τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐν τῷ συνδέσμῳ τῆς εἰρήνης

passages.text: There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called; one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father of all.
God is over all people.
God works through all people.
God is in all people.
There is one body.
There is one Spirit.
God called you to one hope.
There is one Lord.
There is one faith.
There is one baptism.
passages.original: ἓν σῶμα καὶ ἓν Πνεῦμα καθὼς καὶ ἐκλήθητε ἐν μιᾷ ἐλπίδι τῆς κλήσεως ὑμῶν εἷς Κύριος μία πίστις ἓν βάπτισμα εἷς Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ πάντων ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν

passages.text: Now to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Christ gives gifts to people.
Christ gives a different gift to each person.
Christ gives grace to each one of us.
Christ decides how much grace each person receives.
Christ gives grace according to His own gift.
passages.original: Ἑνὶ δὲ ἑκάστῳ ἡμῶν ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις κατὰ τὸ μέτρον τῆς δωρεᾶς τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: This is why it says: “When He ascended on high, He led captives away, and gave gifts to men.”
passages.sermon:
God acted with power.
He ascended to a high place.
He took captives with Him.
He gave gifts to people.
passages.original: διὸ λέγει Ἀναβὰς εἰς ὕψος ᾐχμαλώτευσεν αἰχμαλωσίαν καὶ ἔδωκεν δόματα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις

passages.text: What does “He ascended” mean, except that He also descended to the lower parts of the earth?
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the subject.
Jesus Christ ascended.
“He ascended” means He also descended.
He descended to the lower parts of the earth.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ Ἀνέβη τί ἐστιν εἰ μὴ ὅτι καὶ κατέβη εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς

passages.text: He who descended is the very One who ascended above all the heavens, in order to fill all things.
passages.sermon: Jesus Christ is the One who descended.\r\nJesus Christ is also the One who ascended above all the heavens.\r\nJesus Christ did this to fill all things.
passages.original: ὁ καταβὰς αὐτός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἀναβὰς ὑπεράνω πάντων τῶν οὐρανῶν ἵνα πληρώσῃ τὰ πάντα

passages.text: And it was He who gave some to be apostles, some to be prophets, some to be evangelists, and some to be pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for works of ministry and to build up the body of Christ, until we all reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God, as we mature to the full measure of the stature of Christ.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ gave gifts to His people.
He gave some people to be apostles.
He gave some people to be prophets.
He gave some people to be evangelists.
He gave some people to be pastors and teachers.
He gave these people to equip the saints.
The saints are all believers in Christ.
He equips the saints for works of ministry.
He equips the saints to build up the body of Christ.
The body of Christ is the church.
He does this so that all believers will reach unity in the faith.
He does this so that all believers will reach unity in the knowledge of the Son of God.
He does this so that all believers will become mature.
He wants all believers to reach the full measure of the stature of Christ.
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἔδωκεν τοὺς μὲν ἀποστόλους τοὺς δὲ προφήτας τοὺς δὲ εὐαγγελιστάς τοὺς δὲ ποιμένας καὶ διδασκάλους πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμὸν τῶν ἁγίων εἰς ἔργον διακονίας εἰς οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ μέχρι καταντήσωμεν οἱ πάντες εἰς τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς πίστεως καὶ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς ἄνδρα τέλειον εἰς μέτρον ἡλικίας τοῦ πληρώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Then we will no longer be infants, tossed about by the waves and carried around by every wind of teaching and by the clever cunning of men in their deceitful scheming.
passages.sermon:
We will not be infants anymore.
Infants are easily tossed by waves.
Infants are carried around by every wind of teaching.
Some men use clever tricks.
Some men use deceitful plans.
These men try to lead others astray.
We will not be moved by their teaching or their schemes.
passages.original: ἵνα μηκέτι ὦμεν νήπιοι κλυδωνιζόμενοι καὶ περιφερόμενοι παντὶ ἀνέμῳ τῆς διδασκαλίας ἐν τῇ κυβείᾳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐν πανουργίᾳ πρὸς τὴν μεθοδείαν τῆς πλάνης

passages.text: Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will in all things grow up into Christ Himself, who is the head.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the head.
We speak the truth in love.
We grow up in every way into Christ.
We do this in all things.
passages.original: ἀληθεύοντες δὲ ἐν ἀγάπῃ αὐξήσωμεν εἰς αὐτὸν τὰ πάντα ὅς ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλή Χριστός

passages.text: From Him the whole body, fitted and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love through the work of each individual part.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the head of the body.
The whole body comes from Him.
The body is the church.
Every part of the body fits together.
Every part is held together by every supporting ligament.
Each part works as God gives it strength.
Each part does its own work.
The body grows because of this work.
The body builds itself up in love.
passages.original: ἐξ οὗ πᾶν τὸ σῶμα συναρμολογούμενον καὶ συμβιβαζόμενον διὰ πάσης ἁφῆς τῆς ἐπιχορηγίας κατ’ ἐνέργειαν ἐν μέτρῳ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου μέρους τὴν αὔξησιν τοῦ σώματος ποιεῖται εἰς οἰκοδομὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ

passages.text: So I tell you this, and insist on it in the Lord, that you must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their thinking.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Ephesus.
Paul speaks with authority from the Lord.
Paul gives a command.
Paul says, “You must not live like the Gentiles.”
The Gentiles do not know God.
The Gentiles live in the futility of their thinking.
Their thoughts are empty and useless.
Paul insists that believers must live differently.
passages.original: Τοῦτο οὖν λέγω καὶ μαρτύρομαι ἐν Κυρίῳ μηκέτι ὑμᾶς περιπατεῖν καθὼς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη περιπατεῖ ἐν ματαιότητι τοῦ νοὸς αὐτῶν

passages.text: They are darkened in their understanding and alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them due to the hardness of their hearts.
passages.sermon:
Paul describes the Gentiles.
The Gentiles do not know God.
Their understanding is darkened.
They are separated from the life that comes from God.
They do not know God because they are ignorant.
Their ignorance comes from the hardness of their hearts.
passages.original: ἐσκοτωμένοι τῇ διανοίᾳ ὄντες ἀπηλλοτριωμένοι τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τὴν οὖσαν ἐν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὴν πώρωσιν τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν

passages.text: Having lost all sense of shame, they have given themselves over to sensuality for the practice of every kind of impurity, with a craving for more.
passages.sermon:
The Gentiles have lost all sense of shame.
They have given themselves over to sensuality.
They practice every kind of impurity.
They do this with a constant craving for more.
passages.original: οἵτινες ἀπηλγηκότες ἑαυτοὺς παρέδωκαν τῇ ἀσελγείᾳ εἰς ἐργασίαν ἀκαθαρσίας πάσης ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ

passages.text: But this is not the way you came to know Christ.
passages.sermon: You know Christ in a different way.\r\nYou did not learn Christ in this way.\r\nYour understanding of Christ is not like theirs.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἐμάθετε τὸν Χριστόν

passages.text: Surely you heard of Him and were taught in Him—in keeping with the truth that is in Jesus— to put off your former way of life, your old self, which is being corrupted by its deceitful desires; to be renewed in the spirit of your minds; and to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.
passages.sermon:
You have heard about Jesus.
You have been taught in Jesus.
The truth is in Jesus.
You must put off your former way of life.
Your old self is being corrupted by deceitful desires.
You must be renewed in the spirit of your minds.
You must put on the new self.
God created the new self to be like Him.
The new self is righteous and holy in the truth.
passages.original: εἴ γε αὐτὸν ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐδιδάχθητε καθώς ἐστιν ἀλήθεια ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀποθέσθαι ὑμᾶς κατὰ τὴν προτέραν ἀναστροφὴν τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν φθειρόμενον κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ἀπάτης ἀνανεοῦσθαι δὲ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ νοὸς ὑμῶν καὶ ἐνδύσασθαι τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν κατὰ Θεὸν κτισθέντα ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ὁσιότητι τῆς ἀληθείας

passages.text: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor, for we are all members of one another.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Ephesus.
He teaches them how to live as followers of Jesus.
He says, “Put away all lies.”
Each person must speak the truth to his neighbor.
We are all members of one body.
We belong to each other.
passages.original: Διὸ ἀποθέμενοι τὸ ψεῦδος λαλεῖτε ἀλήθειαν ἕκαστος μετὰ τοῦ πλησίον αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐσμὲν ἀλλήλων μέλη

passages.text: “Be angry, yet do not sin.” Do not let the sun set upon your anger, and do not give the devil a foothold.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Ephesus.
He teaches them how to live as followers of Jesus.
Paul says, “Be angry.”
But do not sin when you are angry.
Do not let your anger last until sunset.
Do not give the devil a chance to work in your life.
passages.original: Ὀργίζεσθε καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐπιδυέτω ἐπὶ τῷ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν μηδὲ δίδοτε τόπον τῷ διαβόλῳ

passages.text: He who has been stealing must steal no longer, but must work, doing good with his own hands, that he may have something to share with the one in need.
passages.sermon:
A person who steals must stop stealing.
He must not take what is not his.
Instead, he must work.
He must use his own hands to do good work.
He must earn what he needs by honest effort.
He must do this so he can share with someone who is in need.
passages.original: Ὁ κλέπτων μηκέτι κλεπτέτω μᾶλλον δὲ κοπιάτω ἐργαζόμενος ταῖς ἰδίαις χερσὶν τὸ ἀγαθόν ἵνα ἔχῃ μεταδιδόναι τῷ χρείαν ἔχοντι

passages.text: Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths, but only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Christians in Ephesus.
Paul told them how to live as followers of Jesus.
Do not let any unwholesome words come out of your mouth.
Speak only words that are good.
Speak words that help build up someone in need.
Let your words give grace to those who hear.
passages.original: Πᾶς λόγος σαπρὸς ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκπορευέσθω ἀλλὰ εἴ τις ἀγαθὸς πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χρείας ἵνα δῷ χάριν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν

passages.text: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit is God.
God gave you the Holy Spirit.
God sealed you with the Holy Spirit.
God sealed you for the day of redemption.
Do not grieve the Holy Spirit.
passages.original: Καὶ μὴ λυπεῖτε τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν ᾧ ἐσφραγίσθητε εἰς ἡμέραν ἀπολυτρώσεως

passages.text: Get rid of all bitterness, rage and anger, outcry and slander, along with every form of malice.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Ephesus.
He tells them to remove all bitterness from their lives.
He tells them to remove all rage.
He tells them to remove all anger.
He tells them to remove all outcry.
He tells them to remove all slander.
He tells them to remove every form of malice.
He commands them to get rid of these things completely.
passages.original: Πᾶσα πικρία καὶ θυμὸς καὶ ὀργὴ καὶ κραυγὴ καὶ βλασφημία ἀρθήτω ἀφ’ ὑμῶν σὺν πάσῃ κακίᾳ

passages.text: Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other just as in Christ God forgave you.
passages.sermon:
God forgave you in Christ.
God showed you mercy through Jesus Christ.
You must forgive each other.
You must be kind to one another.
You must show compassion to one another.
passages.original: γίνεσθε δὲ εἰς ἀλλήλους χρηστοί εὔσπλαγχνοι χαριζόμενοι ἑαυτοῖς καθὼς καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἐν Χριστῷ ἐχαρίσατο ὑμῖν
